greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ λιμὸς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς χωρὶς τοῦ λιμοῦ τοῦ πρότερον, ὃς ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τῷ Αβρααμ· ἐπορεύθη δὲ Ισαακ πρὸς Αβιμελεχ βασιλέα Φυλιστιιμ εἰς Γεραρα.
hint: A famine comes on the land, besides the earlier famine in Abraham's time; Isaac goes to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

notes.text: χωρίς is first *separately, asunder, apart*; πρότερος, the positive Middle Liddell heads, with the repeated article.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐγενήθη for the second ἐγένετο, and τοῦ for the second τῷ, where the Berlin papyrus, 911, has τῷ.

hint: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; to you and to your offspring I will give all this land, and I will keep the oath I swore to Abraham your father.

notes.text: ἵστημι, the chain of GEN 6:18; ὅρκος, the chain of 21:14, in the accusative.

reading: and [[went away|went away, departed from, departed, departed from life]] [[from that place|from that place, thence, thereafter, next]] [[name:Ισαακ]] and [[put down|put down, destroyed, dissolved and broke up, deposed, dismissed and disbanded, neglected, ended and brought to an end, broke, made peace with, unloosed and unyoked, took down, took up his quarters and lodged, went and lodged, took his rest]] [[in the ravine|within, inside of, and by means of the ravine, the chasm, the gully, the mountain-stream]] [[name:Γεραρων]] and [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[there|there, in that place]].

greek: καὶ πάλιν Ισαακ ὤρυξεν τὰ φρέατα τοῦ ὕδατος, ἃ ὤρυξαν οἱ παῖδες Αβρααμ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐνέφραξαν αὐτὰ οἱ Φυλιστιιμ μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν Αβρααμ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπωνόμασεν αὐτοῖς ὀνόματα κατὰ τὰ ὀνόματα, ἃ ἐπωνόμασεν Αβρααμ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Isaac digs again the wells of water that his father Abraham's servants dug, which the Philistines blocked after Abraham his father died, and gives them the names his father gave them.

notes.text: αὐτοῖς is the wells, neuter.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the second ἐπωνόμασεν, which the Berlin papyrus, 911, has.

reading: and [[back|back, again, once more, over again]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[dug|dug, dug through, dug up]] [[the wells|the wells, the tanks and cisterns and reservoirs, the oil jars]] of the water, which [[dug|dug, dug through, dug up]] [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather]] of him and [[blocked up|blocked up]] them [[name:Φυλιστιιμ]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[to die off|to die off, to die, to be put to death, to be slain]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] the father of him, and [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] to them [[names|names, fames, mere names, phrases and expressions]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon]] [[the names|the names, the fames, the mere names, the phrases and expressions]], which [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] the father of him.

greek: καὶ ὤρυξαν οἱ παῖδες Ισαακ ἐν τῇ φάραγγι Γεραρων καὶ εὗρον ἐκεῖ φρέαρ ὕδατος ζῶντος.
hint: Isaac's servants dig in the valley of Gerar and find there a well of living water.

notes.text: ζάω, the chain of GEN 3:22: water that lives, running water.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ὤρυξαν δέ.

reading: and [[dug|dug, dug through, dug up]] [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[in the ravine|within, inside of, and by means of the ravine, the chasm, the gully, the mountain-stream]] [[name:Γεραρων]] and [[found|found, found out, discovered]] [[there|there, in that place]] well of water [[living|living, being in full life and strength, being fresh and strong]].

greek: καὶ ἐμαχέσαντο οἱ ποιμένες Γεραρων μετὰ τῶν ποιμένων Ισαακ φάσκοντες αὐτῶν εἶναι τὸ ὕδωρ· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ φρέατος Ἀδικία· ἠδίκησαν γὰρ αὐτόν.
hint: The shepherds of Gerar quarrel with Isaac's shepherds, saying the water is theirs; he calls the well's name Injustice, because they wronged him.

notes.text: The Greek word ἀδικία printed as the well's name: the Hebrew is ʿĒśeq, *contention*.
φάσκω, *to say, affirm, assert*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds ἐκείνου; the Berlin papyrus, 911, does not.

names.gloss: (Ἀδικία, the Greek word ἀδικία, "wrong-doing, injustice", printed as the well's name; the Hebrew is ʿĒśeq, "contention")

greek: ἀπάρας δὲ Ισαακ ἐκεῖθεν ὤρυξεν φρέαρ ἕτερον, ἐκρίνοντο δὲ καὶ περὶ ἐκείνου· καὶ ἐπωνόμασεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐχθρία.
hint: He moves on and digs another well; they quarrel over that one too, and he names it Enmity.

notes.text: κρίνω in the middle, *to be separated, to be judged*: of a dispute.
καί as *also*, plain, as at 19:21.

names.gloss: (Ἐχθρία, the Greek word ἐχθρία, "hatred, enmity", printed as the well's name; the Hebrew is Śiṭnâ, "accusation")

greek: ἀπάρας δὲ ἐκεῖθεν ὤρυξεν φρέαρ ἕτερον, καὶ οὐκ ἐμαχέσαντο περὶ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἐπωνόμασεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Εὐρυχωρία λέγων Διότι νῦν ἐπλάτυνεν κύριος ἡμῖν καὶ ηὔξησεν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: He moves on and digs another well, and over that one they do not quarrel; he names it Room, saying: Now the Lord has made room for us and increased us on the earth.

notes.text: The Greek word εὐρυχωρία, *open space, free room*, printed as the well's name; the Hebrew is Rĕḥōbôt.
πλατύνω, one sense, *to make broad, widen, enlarge*; the aorist, with ηὔξησεν beside it.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[having lifted off|having lifted off, having taken away and carried off, having removed, having set off and departed, having marched away]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[from that place|from that place, thence, thereafter, next]] [[dug|dug, dug through, dug up]] well [[other|other, one of two, the other of two, another, second, different, other than, worse]], and not [[fought|fought, fought with, quarrelled and wrangled and disputed, opposed and gainsaid, contended for the mastery]] [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very]] of it; and [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] of it [[name:Εὐρυχωρία]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]] [[for the reason that|for the reason that, since, wherefore and for what reason, that]] [[now|now, even now, just now]] [[made broad|made broad, widened, enlarged]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] to us and [[made large|made large, increased, augmented, increased in power and strengthened and exalted and aggrandised, promoted to honour and glorified and magnified]] us [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

names.gloss: (Εὐρυχωρία, the Greek word εὐρυχωρία, "open space, free room", printed as the well's name; the Hebrew is Rĕḥōbôt, "broad places")

greek: Ἀνέβη δὲ ἐκεῖθεν ἐπὶ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ ὅρκου.
hint: He goes up from there to the Well of the Oath.

notes.text: As at 21:31, the well named by the oath sworn there.

reading: [[went up|went up, mounted, went up to, embarked]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[from that place|from that place, thence, thereafter, next]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the well|the well, the tank and cistern and reservoir, the oil jar]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath]].

greek: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτῷ κύριος ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ καὶ εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς Αβρααμ τοῦ πατρός σου· μὴ φοβοῦ· μετὰ σοῦ γάρ εἰμι καὶ ηὐλόγηκά σε καὶ πληθυνῶ τὸ σπέρμα σου διὰ Αβρααμ τὸν πατέρα σου.
hint: The Lord appears to him that night and says: I am the God of Abraham your father; do not be afraid, for I am with you, and I have blessed you and will multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham your father.

notes.text: The perfect of εὐλογέω, with the standing result.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads εὐλογήσω, the future; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has the perfect.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[was seen|was seen, was looked at, was beheld and perceived and observed, was looked out for]] to him [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[in the night-season|within, inside of, and by means of the night-season, the night, the watches of the night, the dark of night, the night of death]] [[that|that, in order that]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] I am [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather]] of you; not [[be put to flight|be put to flight, flee affrighted, flee, be seized with fear, be affrighted, fear]]; [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you for I am and [[I have spoken well of|I have spoken well of and it stands so, I have praised and it stands so, I have honoured and it stands so, I have blessed and it stands so]] you and [[I will make full|I will make full, I will increase, I will multiply]] [[that which is sown|that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent]] of you [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] the father of you.

greek: καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου καὶ ἔπηξεν ἐκεῖ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ· ὤρυξαν δὲ ἐκεῖ οἱ παῖδες Ισαακ φρέαρ.
hint: He builds an altar there and calls on the name of the Lord, and pitches his tent there; and his servants dig a well.

notes.text: πήγνυμι is first *to make fast*.

reading: and [[built a house|built a house, built, built for himself]] [[there|there, in that place]] an altar and [[called upon|called upon, invoked and appealed to, invited, called in as a helper, was called by surname]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]] and [[made fast|made fast, fixed in the earth and planted, fastened together and constructed and built, made solid and stiff and hard, froze, became solid and stiff, became congealed and froze]] [[there|there, in that place]] [[the covered place|the covered place, the tent, the camp, the dwelling-place, the temple]] of him; [[dug|dug, dug through, dug up]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[there|there, in that place]] [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids]] [[name:Ισαακ]] well.

hint: Abimelech comes to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his groomsman and Phicol the commander of his forces.

notes.text: As at 21:22: νυμφαγωγός, one sense, *leader of the bride*; ἀρχιστράτηγος, LSJ, *commander-in-chief*.

hint: Isaac says to them: Why have you come to me? You hated me and sent me away from you.

notes.text: *Why*, the ellipsis ἵνα τί γένηται, as at 12:19.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

hint: They say: We have seen plainly that the Lord was with you, and we said, Let there be an oath between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,

Capitalised because each opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

greek: μὴ ποιήσειν μεθʼ ἡμῶν κακόν, καθότι ἡμεῖς σε οὐκ ἐβδελυξάμεθα, καὶ ὃν τρόπον ἐχρησάμεθά σοι καλῶς καὶ ἐξαπεστείλαμέν σε μετʼ εἰρήνης· καὶ νῦν σὺ εὐλογητὸς ὑπὸ κυρίου.
hint: that you will do us no harm, just as we did not abhor you, and as we treated you well and sent you away in peace; and now you are blessed by the Lord.

greek: καὶ ἀναστάντες τὸ πρωὶ ὤμοσαν ἄνθρωπος τῷ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς Ισαακ, καὶ ἀπῴχοντο ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ μετὰ σωτηρίας.
hint: and rising early they swear to one another; Isaac sends them off, and they go from him in safety.

notes.text: *A man to his neighbour*, the Hebrew idiom *ʾîš lĕrēʿēhû*; πλησίον after the article, as at 11:3.
ἀποίχομαι, *to be gone away, be absent*.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ παραγενόμενοι οἱ παῖδες Ισαακ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ περὶ τοῦ φρέατος, οὗ ὤρυξαν, καὶ εἶπαν Οὐχ εὕρομεν ὕδωρ.
hint: That same day Isaac's servants come and tell him about the well they had dug, and say: We have not found water.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸ Ὅρκος· διὰ τοῦτο ὄνομα τῇ πόλει Φρέαρ ὅρκου ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited]] it [[name:Ὅρκος]]; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the city|to the city, to the citadel, to the country, to the body of citizens, to the state]] [[name:Φρέαρ]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] the to-day [[of day|of day, of day-break, of time]].

(Φρέαρ ὅρκου, "well of the oath", the Greek of Hebrew Bĕʾēr Šebaʿ, Beersheba)

greek: Ἦν δὲ Ησαυ ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα καὶ ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα Ιουδιν τὴν θυγατέρα Βεηρ τοῦ Χετταίου καὶ τὴν Βασεμμαθ θυγατέρα Αιλων τοῦ Ευαίου.
hint: Esau was forty years old when he took as wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hivite.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the first τήν and reads μασεμμαθ and αιλωμ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has ευλων for Αιλων.

(Ιουδιν, for Hebrew Yĕhûdît, "Jewess" or "woman of Judah")
(Βεηρ, for Hebrew Bĕʾērî, usually connected with bĕʾēr, "well")

greek: καὶ ἦσαν ἐρίζουσαι τῷ Ισαακ καὶ τῇ Ρεβεκκα.
hint: And they were a strife to Isaac and to Rebekah.

notes.text: ἦν with the participle, the formula in its shorter form; ἐρίζω is first *to strive, wrangle, quarrel*.

reading: and were, and kept on being, [[striving|striving, wrangling, quarrelling, rivalling and vying with and being a match for, contending with, engaging in a contest and keeping the contest up]] to [[name:Ισαακ]] and to [[name:Ρεβεκκα]].
